Keywords: engagement comments discussion question community conversation reply
Example: I've been posting on LinkedIn for 3 years. This single change doubled my engagement overnight. [Value] What posting change made the biggest difference for you?
Do: End with a specific, easy-to-answer question. Make readers feel like their opinion matters. Reply to every comment in the first hour.
Dont: Don't ask generic 'thoughts?' Don't make the question too broad. Don't ignore comments (algorithm punishes you).
CTA Options: What's your take? / Drop a [emoji] if you agree / Tell me in the comments / What's worked for you?

Keywords: save bookmark valuable resource tips list educational reference
Formula: [Educational hook] + [Numbered list or structured value] + 'Save this for later'
Example: 5 caption formulas that get 3x more saves: [1. ...] [2. ...] [3. ...] [4. ...] [5. ...] Save this for when you need to write a post.
Do: Structure content as a reference (numbered, bulleted). Include 'Save this' explicitly. Teach something with lasting value.
Dont: Don't ask for saves on fluffy content. Don't use 'Save this' without giving a reason. Don't use this on opinion posts.
CTA Options: Save this for later / Bookmark this / Screenshot this / You'll want to come back to this

Keywords: bio profile visit click through visibility brand awareness new audience
Formula: [Intriguing hook about who you are] + [Value you provide] + [Soft CTA to profile]
Example: I help DTC brands turn Instagram views into revenue without running a single ad. If that's you, follow along — I post strategies every weekday.
Do: State exactly who you help and how. Give a compelling reason to follow. Use on viral posts to convert viewers to followers.
Dont: Don't be vague about what you do. Don't make it all about you — frame it as value to them. Don't use on every post (seems desperate).
CTA Options: Check my profile for more / Follow for daily [topic] / Click my bio link / See my full strategy in my profile

Keywords: website link click bio traffic drive conversion lead capture
Formula: [Pain point hook] + [Value tease] + [Clear benefit to clicking]
Example: Most landing pages convert at 1-2%. But these 5 changes can push yours past 8%. Full breakdown with examples in the link in bio.
Do: Tell them exactly what they'll get when they click. Create a gap between what the post says and what the link delivers (tease).
Dont: Don't say 'link in bio' without telling them WHY to click. Don't send to a homepage — send to a specific landing page. Don't overuse this CTA.
CTA Options: Link in bio / Full guide in bio / See the breakdown → link in bio / Free download at link in bio

Keywords: story narrative personal brand authentic emotional connection human
Example: When I started my agency, I lost our biggest client on day 30. $15k/month gone. No savings. Here's how we recovered and what I learned about client retention. [Story] Lesson: ...
Do: Use real emotions and specific details. Include unexpected turns. End with a clear takeaway. Be vulnerable — it builds trust.
Dont: Don't tell stories that don't have a lesson or point. Don't use vague language ('things were hard'). Don't make it too long on Twitter.
CTA Options: Share your story below / What's your lesson from failure? / Have you been through this? / Drop a comment

Keywords: education how to teach tutorial tip guide learn skill practical
Example: How to write a LinkedIn post that gets 10,000 views: Step 1: Hook (first line must stop the scroll) Step 2: ... [Structured value] Try this framework on your next post.
Do: Be specific and actionable. Use numbered steps or bullet points. Test the advice before sharing it. Keep steps simple.
Dont: Don't share untested advice. Don't make steps too abstract. Don't forget to relate it back to their goal at the end.
CTA Options: Try this today / Which step do you struggle with? / Save this process / Let me know how it goes

Keywords: promotional offer product service announce sell conversion promo launch
Formula: [Pain point they relate to] + [Your solution] + [Social proof] + [Specific CTA with deadline]
Example: Tired of spending hours writing LinkedIn posts that nobody sees? Our content workshop takes you from blank page to viral post in 90 minutes. 200+ marketers have used it. Open for 48 more hours. [Link]
Do: Lead with the problem, not the product. Include urgency or scarcity when real. Show social proof.
Dont: Don't lead with your offer. Don't use vague CTAs. Don't promote without warming up the audience first. Don't run promotions too often (max 20% of posts).
CTA Options: Get [X]% off before [date] / Only [N] spots left / Enroll now / Shop now / Book a call

Keywords: behind the scenes authentic process real raw transparent day in the life
Formula: [Day-in-the-life opening] + [Honest behind-the-scenes look] + [Relatable ending or question]
Example: What my actual Tuesday looked like: 6am: Missed alarm 8am: Client call went off the rails 12pm: Brainstorm that actually worked 9pm: Finally sent that email I'd been avoiding All of it. Real life.
Do: Be genuinely authentic, not 'authenticity theater'. Show process, mistakes, and imperfection. People trust realness over perfection.
Dont: Don't manufacture 'authentic' moments. Don't overshare personal problems unrelated to your audience. Don't use BTS as a disguise for bragging.
CTA Options: Does your day look like this? / What does your real [day/process] look like? / Follow for more real-talk / Save this if you needed to see this today

Keywords: announcement launch new product event update milestone big news reveal
Formula: [Big news statement] + [Why it matters to the reader] + [What to do next]
Example: Huge news: [Product/Feature/Event] is officially live. After 6 months in beta with 200 early testers, we're opening the doors. Here's what it means for you... [CTA]
Do: Lead with the announcement clearly. Explain the reader benefit immediately. Include a specific next step.
Dont: Don't bury the announcement after a long intro. Don't make it only about you — always pivot to what it means for THEM. Don't forget the CTA.
CTA Options: Get early access / Sign up now / Join the waitlist / Learn more / Celebrate with us

Keywords: inspirational motivational mindset quote uplift encourage resilience purpose
Formula: [Bold principle or truth] + [Brief supporting story or context] + [Encouraging close]
Example: Success isn't about being the smartest. It's about staying in the game longer than everyone else. I've watched 'less talented' people consistently outperform because they simply didn't stop. Keep going.
Do: Keep it grounded and real — avoid clichés. Root inspiration in a specific truth. Connect it to your audience's specific journey.
Dont: Don't use generic quotes without adding your unique perspective. Don't be preachy. Don't post inspiration without value-add.
CTA Options: Share if this resonated / Who needed to hear this today? / Save this for hard days / Tag someone who needs this
